newsitem.title: USA: McDermott sees wider fiscal Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: McDermott sees wider fiscal Q4 loss.

text.p: McDermott International Inc said Monday it expects a fourth quarter loss of $180-$200 million, compared with a year-earlier loss of $4 million.
McDermott also said it had begun an investigation into allegations that some former employees may have engaged in wrongdoing. It said the allegations are not related to its fourth-quarter forecast.
McDermott said its majority-owned subsidiary J. Ray McDermott will have a net loss for the fourth quarter of $60-$70 million, compared to a year-earlier loss of $18 million.

McDermott said its fourth quarter results will include a $17 million after-tax gain from the sale of assets, and after-tax charges of about $35 million from surplus and obsolete equipment. Full results will be reported during the third week of May.
The results will also include an after-tax charge of $130 million from an increase in reserves for uninsured asbestos claims and from the carrying values of various assets.
The company said it recently learned of allegations of wrongdoing by some former employees of McDermott International and J. Ray McDermott.
If true, the allegations could result in civil and/or criminal liability for the companies, it said. Both companies have begun an internal investigation and retained outside counsel to assist them.
McDermott declined to provide details about the allegations but said more information may be available later today.
McDermott is an energy services company.
